content.text: The redline validated cleanly. Submitting the finding.

input.quote: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.
input.rationale: Section 11 (Severability; Governing Law) selects Arizona law, which is outside the playbook's accepted list of New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales, so the clause fails both the preferred and the fallback positions on a material term. Arizona is also effectively the Contractor-favorable choice here, with no offsetting benefit to us. Separately, the Agreement contains no forum, venue, or jurisdiction provision anywhere (searches for jurisdiction, venue, arbitration and courts returned nothing, and the preamble contains only entity recitals), leaving the dispute forum entirely unspecified; there is at least no mandatory arbitration seated abroad, so this is a deviation rather than walk-away territory. Consistent with the redline guidance to change only the jurisdiction words and forum, the proposed edit swaps "Arizona" for "the State of New York" and appends an exclusive-jurisdiction sentence for the state and federal courts in New York County, reaching the preferred position while leaving the severability language and the conflict-of-laws carve-out intact. The comment offers Delaware, California, or England and Wales with the courts of London as the fallback if New York is resisted.

proposal.summary: Replace Arizona governing law with New York law and add exclusive venue in New York County courts
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have changed the governing law from Arizona to New York and added exclusive venue in the state and federal courts in New York County, consistent with our playbook's accepted jurisdictions. If New York does not work for you, we can accept Delaware, California, or England and Wales with the courts of London.

ops.newText: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof. The parties irrevocably submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York for any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement.
